From 570e2ccc7cb35fe720106964e65060602d3d2ac4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jianan Huang <huangjianan@xiaomi.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:18:10 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] f2fs: avoid reading already updated pages during GC

We found the following issue during fuzz testing:

page: refcount:3 mapcount:0 mapping:00000000b6e89c65 index:0x18b2dc pfn:0x161ba9
memcg:f8ffff800e269c00
aops:f2fs_meta_aops ino:2
flags: 0x52880000000080a9(locked|waiters|uptodate|lru|private|zone=1|kasantag=0x4a)
raw: 52880000000080a9 fffffffec6e17588 fffffffec0ccc088 a7ffff8067063618
raw: 000000000018b2dc 0000000000000009 00000003ffffffff f8ffff800e269c00
page dumped because: VM_BUG_ON_FOLIO(folio_test_uptodate(folio))
page_owner tracks the page as allocated
 post_alloc_hook+0x58c/0x5ec
 prep_new_page+0x34/0x284
 get_page_from_freelist+0x2dcc/0x2e8c
 __alloc_pages_noprof+0x280/0x76c
 __folio_alloc_noprof+0x18/0xac
 __filemap_get_folio+0x6bc/0xdc4
 pagecache_get_page+0x3c/0x104
 do_garbage_collect+0x5c78/0x77a4
 f2fs_gc+0xd74/0x25f0
 gc_thread_func+0xb28/0x2930
 kthread+0x464/0x5d8
 ret_from_fork+0x10/0x20

diff --git a/fs/f2fs/gc.c b/fs/f2fs/gc.c
index d15e122b470c..80b8500fa987 100644
--- a/fs/f2fs/gc.c
+++ b/fs/f2fs/gc.c
@@ -1231,7 +1231,7 @@ static int ra_data_block(struct inode *inode, pgoff_t index)
 		.encrypted_page = NULL,
 		.in_list = 0,
 	};
-	int err;
+	int err = 0;
 
 	folio = f2fs_grab_cache_folio(mapping, index, true);
 	if (IS_ERR(folio))
@@ -1284,6 +1284,9 @@ static int ra_data_block(struct inode *inode, pgoff_t index)
 
 	fio.encrypted_page = &efolio->page;
 
+	if (folio_test_uptodate(efolio))
+		goto put_encrypted_page;
+
 	err = f2fs_submit_page_bio(&fio);
 	if (err)
 		goto put_encrypted_page;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in f2fs garbage collection where a page that was already up-to-date was being re-read, triggering a `VM_BUG_ON`. The fix is in `ra_data_block()` in `fs/f2fs/gc.c`:

1. **Initialization change**: `err` is now initialized to `0` instead of being uninitialized, ensuring a proper return value when early-exit paths are taken.

2. **Up-to-date check**: After allocating an encrypted page (`efolio`), a new check `if (folio_test_uptodate(efolio))` is added. If the page is already up-to-date, the function jumps to `put_encrypted_page` without submitting a new I/O.

These two changes work together: the early exit via the new check uses the initialized `err = 0` (indicating success) and avoids the bug by not re-reading an already updated page, preventing the assertion failure.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
efolio = f2fs_filemap_get_folio(META_MAPPING(sbi), dn.data_blkaddr,
				FGP_LOCK | FGP_CREAT, GFP_NOFS);
...
fio.encrypted_page = &efolio->page;
...
err = f2fs_submit_page_bio(&fio);
```
Reason:
The code allocates or retrieves an encrypted page (efolio) and submits a read I/O via `f2fs_submit_page_bio` without first checking if the folio is already up-to-date. If the page was already updated (e.g., from a previous GC move that wrote data to that block), the subsequent bio completion triggers `VM_BUG_ON_FOLIO(folio_test_uptodate(folio))` in `folio_end_read` because the kernel expects a read I/O to be initiated only on a non-uptodate page.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
+	if (folio_test_uptodate(efolio))
+		goto put_encrypted_page;
+
 	err = f2fs_submit_page_bio(&fio);
```
Reason:
The added `folio_test_uptodate` check ensures that if the encrypted page is already up-to-date, the read I/O is skipped entirely by jumping to the cleanup label `put_encrypted_page`. This avoids submitting a redundant bio that would cause an inconsistent page state and trigger the VM_BUG_ON. The page already contains the correct data, so no further reads are needed.
